title: Bring It to the Right Place

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Any Israelite who sacrifices an ox, a lamb or a goat in the camp or outside of it instead of bringing it to the entrance to the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD in front of the tabernacle of the LORD — that person shall be considered guilty of bloodshed; they have shed blood and must be cut off from their people." - Lev 17:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The rule is strict. Slaughter an animal anywhere other than the tent of meeting, and you are guilty of bloodshed.

That sounds severe until we understand what was happening. Israel had come out of Egypt and was heading into Canaan, and both were full of altars — shrines on hilltops, sacrifices to local gods, private worship in private places. God was closing that door before His people walked through it.

There was one place, because there was one God.

We do not bring animals anywhere today. But the instinct this law addresses is very much alive. We like worship on our own terms — private, unaccountable, arranged to suit us. Faith that never has to sit under anyone's teaching, never has to be questioned, never has to show up.

Scripture keeps pulling us back towards the gathered people of God. Let us not give up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing (Heb 10:25). Not because buildings are holy, but because faith that answers to no one drifts.

Jesus said something remarkable about this: where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them (Matt 18:20). The meeting place has changed. The principle has not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has your faith become entirely private and unaccountable?
2. What do you gain from worshipping with others that you cannot get alone?
3. Is there a step back towards God's people you need to take?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from a faith that answers to no one. Give me a real place among Your people, and help me value gathering with them. Amen.
